title: Degrees Longitude to Kilometers Calculator
description: Convert degrees of longitude to kilometres at your latitude with the Degrees Longitude to Kilometers Calculator — cosine honesty included. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, one degree of longitude is 111.319 km at the equator but only 55.8 km at 60° — and in New York it is 84.4 km, the number that decides whether a 'degree away' is a day trip or a commute.
quick_answer: The Degrees Longitude to Kilometers Calculator converts a difference in longitude into the east-west ground distance it represents at a given latitude, applying the cosine shrinkage that makes longitude the treacherous axis. Enter the degrees and the latitude and read the true distance in kilometres or miles.

Departure and longitude-run calculations from the sailing tradition — the east-west component of a course, priced.
1° of longitude: 111.319 km (equator) → 84.442 (New York) → 78.847 (45°) → 55.800 (60°) → 0 at the pole, where all meridians marry. No other everyday unit dies at its destination like this.
The idealised 15° zone spans 1,265 km of ground at New York's latitude (15 × 84.44) — wider than most countries, which is why zone borders bend around politics instead.

popular_table.note: The quick rule — equatorial length × cos(latitude) — matches the ellipsoid within a fraction of a percent; the calculator uses the ellipsoid itself.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
East-west ground distance for a longitude difference at a stated latitude, using WGS84's prime-vertical radius — the ellipsoid's own answer, not just the cosine rule.
Do I need an account?
No — degrees and latitude in, distance out.
Can I use the result for professional work?
The geometry is ellipsoid-true — planning, reporting and checking stand on it. Survey practice governs legal measurement, as always.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — the frame GPS produces and web maps consume.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — resolution is not accuracy; the precision tools on this site price each decimal place in metres.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Distances are numbers for any system; coordinate pairs paste as themselves.
Why must latitude be given?
Because the answer does not exist without it — a degree of longitude is a different distance at every latitude. Any source quoting one fixed number is quoting the equator and hoping.
At the pole?
Zero — longitude itself dissolves there, and the calculator's honest limit is the geography's.
Spans crossing the date line?
Take the smaller arc (a span from 179° to −179° is 2°, not 358°) — the calculator expects the true difference; the Span tools unwrap sets automatically.
Solar time relation?
Earth turns 15° per hour; at your latitude the converter prices that hour in kilometres — astronomy with a ground address.
Feet?
Kilometres and miles carry the page; the numbers convert onward trivially.
